teardown_clusters.cluster_name: South Dallas / Fair Park Systemic Teardown-Replace Corridor
teardown_clusters.evidence_type: City-adopted area plan explicitly documenting teardown-replace pattern as primary redevelopment mechanism
teardown_clusters.evidence_summary: The South Dallas/Fair Park Area Plan (SDFP), adopted by Dallas City Council June 25, 2025, was triggered by four years of documented 'grossly incompatible' infill construction. Residents describe three-story flat-roof homes with large driveways being built on teardown sites. The plan explicitly cites this as the dominant redevelopment pattern in existing single-family blocks and proposes design standards to govern future infill teardown-rebuilds.
teardown_clusters.regulatory_response: SDFP Area Plan adopted June 25, 2025. Provisions: Neighborhood Mixed-Use rezoning on 2nd Avenue corridor; ADU overlay district rights; duplex subdivision rights; Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area designation (federal HUD funds).
teardown_clusters.amara_os_targeting_priority: TIER 1 — Highest priority. City regulatory response confirms systemic teardown wave. Active lot shortage forming.

teardown_clusters.cluster_name: Tenth Street Historic District Systematic Teardown Cluster
teardown_clusters.evidence_type: Litigated demolition record; documented percentage teardown rate within landmark district
teardown_clusters.evidence_summary: Between 2010 and 2023, the city documented 35 demolished historic homes in the Tenth Street Landmark District. A 2019 lawsuit alleged the real figure was closer to 72 demolitions out of 260 total homes — a 28% teardown rate in the district. Mechanism: Dallas's '3,000-square-foot rule' (passed 2010) permits demolition of homes smaller than 3,000 sq ft within a Landmark District without full Landmark Commission review, enabling fast-tracked teardown-infill cycles.
teardown_clusters.teardown_rate: 28%+ (72 of 260 homes per lawsuit allegation; 35 per city records)
teardown_clusters.enabling_mechanism: Dallas 3,000-sq-ft demolition rule (2010) — allows demo of sub-3,000 sq ft homes in landmark districts without full Commission review
teardown_clusters.amara_os_targeting_priority: TIER 1 — High priority. Documented systematic pattern. Sub-3000 sq ft homes still present = continued teardown risk = lot supply opportunity.

teardown_clusters.cluster_name: West Dallas / Los Altos / Trinity Groves Multi-Parcel Demo Assemblage
teardown_clusters.evidence_type: Named developer / named properties / sequential demolition / documented ground-up redevelopment
teardown_clusters.evidence_summary: Developer Jackson acquired four adjacent commercial properties (former Barrow Filling Station, West Dallas Pharmacy, Chuyitas Taqueria, tire shop) in 2019 on Singleton Blvd at N Winnetka Ave. Asbestos abatement and sequential demolitions ran through 2024. Site then sold to Frank Nuchereno / Hello! Deluxe Car Wash. Ground-up construction active mid-2025. A broader wave of demolition-linked gentrification documented across West Dallas with Dallas Free Press covering multiple displacement events. Goldenrod Companies separately acquired ~90 parcels (~45 acres) in Trinity Groves in 2023 from West Dallas Investments LLC.
teardown_clusters.amara_os_targeting_priority: TIER 2 — High value but large institutional players dominate. Smaller scattered lots around the Goldenrod assemblage edge may be AMARA OS targets.

teardown_clusters.cluster_name: North Oak Cliff / Bishop Arts Cleared-Lot Townhome Pipeline
teardown_clusters.evidence_type: Active MLS listings of permit-approved cleared townhome assemblages; Redfin active land inventory data
teardown_clusters.evidence_summary: Current listing data documents multiple shovel-ready, permit-approved townhome assemblages actively marketed to builders: a 14-townhome permitted project in Bishop Arts; a 16-unit permitted corner-lot assemblage (3+ contiguous lots); a 16-townhome project at 316 and 324 N Lancaster. Redfin shows 139 active land listings in Oak Cliff at median $310K. Recent month sales: 32 condos, 15 townhouses, 12 multi-family units — indicating active build-out of cleared lots.
active_pipeline: 16-unit permitted corner-lot assemblage (3+ contiguous lots) — Oak Cliff
16-townhome project at 316 and 324 N Lancaster Ave
teardown_clusters.land_inventory: 139 active land listings per Redfin; median $310K
teardown_clusters.amara_os_targeting_priority: TIER 2 — Active townhome demand confirmed but land prices elevated ($310K median). Watch for off-market lots adjacent to permit-approved assemblages.

teardown_clusters.cluster_name: West Oak Cliff Hampton-Clarendon Corridor Emerging Redevelopment Zone
teardown_clusters.evidence_type: City rezoning action (August 2025) — 35.25 acres to mixed-use/multifamily; cascading WOCAP-driven rezoning since 2022
teardown_clusters.evidence_summary: Dallas City Council voted 12-3 on August 13, 2025 to rezone 35.25 acres at Hampton Road and Clarendon Drive intersection. WOCAP (adopted 2022) has spawned: Downtown Elmwood authorized hearing (January 2024); Jimtown authorized hearing (January 2025); Hampton-Clarendon (August 2025). Additional 3.2-acre apartment rezoning in Oak Cliff approved April 2026 citing ForwardDallas 2.0 and 2025 Texas state law.
teardown_clusters.regulatory_driver: West Oak Cliff Area Plan (WOCAP) — adopted 2022; producing cascading rezoning authorizations through 2025-2026
teardown_clusters.amara_os_targeting_priority: TIER 2 — Rezoning pipeline active. Auto-oriented parcels converting to mixed-use = infill opportunity. Watch for adjacent vacant/underutilized lots.
